turns.content: Foo Medical's diabetes dashboard shows HbA1c control (share of type 2 diabetes patients' HbA1c results under 7%) dropping. Find out why, back every claim with SQL, and check the rest of the data for other problems that would distort a dashboard. Data is the local synthetic analytics pack.

REPLAY (no key)

I will measure monthly HbA1c control for type 2 diabetes (SNOMED 44054006) without assuming a unit, then split the same results by units. A jump in the average together with a new unit is a unit change, not a clinical change. The corrected value uses the IFCC conversion mmol/mol to NGSP percent: value / 10.929 + 2.15.

queries.sql: select date_trunc('month', date)::date as month, count(*) as n, round(avg(value_num), 2) as avg_value, round(100.0 * avg(case when value_num < 7 then 1 else 0 end), 1) as control_pct, string_agg(distinct units, ',') as units from observations where code = '4548-4' and patient in (select patient from conditions where code = '44054006') and date >= '2025-12-01' and date < '2026-06-01' group by 1 order by 1

select date_trunc('month', date)::date as month, units, count(*) as n, round(avg(value_num), 1) as avg_value from observations where code = '4548-4' and date >= '2025-12-01' and date < '2026-06-01' group by 1, 2 order by 1, 2

select date_trunc('month', date)::date as month, round(100.0 * avg(case when (case when units = 'mmol/mol' then value_num / 10.929 + 2.15 else value_num end) < 7 then 1 else 0 end), 1) as corrected_control_pct, count(*) as n from observations where code = '4548-4' and patient in (select patient from conditions where code = '44054006') and date >= '2025-12-01' and date < '2026-06-01' group by 1 order by 1
select min(date)::date as start_date, count(*) as n from observations where code = '4548-4' and units = 'mmol/mol'
select distinct e.organization as organization_id from observations o join encounters e on e.id = o.encounter where o.code = '4548-4' and o.units = 'mmol/mol' order by 1
